instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, rinse the sticky rice, cover it with at least 1 inch of water and soak it.

Drain the water chestnuts and mince 1/3 cup of them. Mince the ginger and the white parts of the green onions. In a large bowl, mix the pork with the water chestnuts, ginger, green onions, 3 tbsp cold water, the wine, cornstarch, white pepper, sesame oil, salt and sugar.
Stir the mixture in one direction for 5 minutes, until it turns sticky and fluffy. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Drain the soaked rice well and spread it on a plate. Cut parchment to fit your steamer, poke a few holes in it and lay it in the steamer. Fill the pot under it with cold water.

Scoop about 1 tbsp of the pork mixture, roll it into a ball, then roll it in the rice until it is coated all over and press gently so the rice sticks. Set the balls on the parchment about 1/2 inch apart, since the rice swells as it cooks. You should get about 30.

Cover and steam over high heat for 20 minutes. If your steamer holds only half the balls, steam them in two rounds. The meatballs are done when they reach 160°F in the middle. A thermometer is optional. Without one, cut a ball in half: there should be no pink and the rice should be see-through and soft.
Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 3 minutes. Serve hot.
advance_prep_notes: soak the sticky rice at least 2 hours ahead
method_notes: The lead is The Woks of Life (4.94 from 15 ratings, so a fallback lead): pork with water chestnuts, ginger, scallion and Shaoxing wine, stirred in one direction until fluffy, rolled in sticky rice that soaked for 2 hours and steamed for 20 minutes. China Sichuan Food and Eat the Love agree on soaking the rice and steaming, and add egg, soy sauce or oyster sauce. This version uses store-bought ground pork, which The Woks of Life allows, and parchment in place of the bamboo leaves.
